title: Biblioburro, the donkey library
hook: A Colombian teacher takes books to remote villages on two donkeys.
peek: For years a schoolteacher in northern Colombia has loaded books onto two donkeys called Alfa and Beto and led them to villages with no library. Children gather to hear him read and borrow books until his next visit.
lede: Luis Soriano is a primary school teacher from La Gloria, a small town in Colombia's Magdalena region. In the late 1990s he noticed that children in the surrounding countryside had almost no books. So he began loading his own collection onto two donkeys and walking them out to remote villages. He called the project Biblioburro, a mix of biblioteca and burro.

bullets.text: Soriano named the donkeys Alfa and Beto, so that together they spell out the start of the word alphabet. One carries books and the other often carries more books, plus the teacher's supplies.
The project reportedly began with about 70 books from Soriano's own shelves. As news spread, donations arrived from around Colombia and abroad, and the collection grew into the thousands.
Soriano usually rides out at weekends, after a week of teaching. When he arrives, children gather to hear him read aloud, help with schoolwork, and choose books to keep until he comes back.

His story has been told in a documentary and in children's picture books, including Jeanette Winter's Biblioburro and Monica Brown's Waiting for the Biblioburro. He later opened a small library building in La Gloria as well.
